layout_dets.text: Critical Potentials for Pitting Corrosion of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ni, Cr-Ni, Cr-Fe, and Related Stainless Steels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: J. Horvath¹ and H. H. Uhlig*

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Department of Metallurgy and Materials Science,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ABSTRACT

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Critical pitting potentials for the binary Cr-Fe and Cr-Ni alloys in 0.1N

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NaCl become more noble (correspondingly more resistant to pitting) with in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creasing Cr content, particularly in the region 25-40% Cr and 10-20% Cr, re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spectively. The potentials for 57.8% Cr-Fe and pure Cr fall within the trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive region. Ni containing 3.2% Mo, to the contrary, shows a lower (more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: active) critical potential; higher per cent Mo-Ni alloys appear to fall within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the transpassive region corroding anodically as MoO₄-- plus Ni+ + without

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting. Ni alloyed with 15% Cr-Fe shifts the potential in the noble direction;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo alloyed with 15% Cr, 13% Ni stainless steel has a similar but even

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: greater effect. At 0°C, 15% Cr, 13% Ni stainless steel exhibits a potential 0.5v

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more noble than at 25°C, corresponding to greatly increased resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting. This shift is less pronounced for the stainless steels containing Mo; in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fact, at or above 1.5% Mo, the critical potentials at 0°C are below those at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 25°Ć. In 0.1N NaBr, alloyed Mo shifts the potentials slightly in the active di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rection, contrary to a marked noble shift in 0.1N NaCl. At 0°C the potentials

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are still more active. These trends correlate with observed pitting for 15% Cr,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 13% Ni stainless steel and the similar alloy containing 2.4% Mo in 10% FeBr3

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both at 0° and 25°C. Absence of pitting is observed in 10% FeCl3 at 0°C for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 15% Cr, 13% Ni stainless steel, but not for the similar alloy containing 2.4%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mo, which pits. The over-all results are explained on the basis of competitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adsorption at the metal surface and an effect of temperature on the structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the double layer.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The concept of a critical potential above which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: passive alloys are liable to pitting corrosion in halide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solutions, but below which they resist pitting, pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sumably for an indefinite period of exposure, has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: described by several investigators. This subject was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reviewed, among others, in an earlier paper by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kolotyrkin (1) and briefly by Leckie and Uhlig (2).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The latter reported the effect of various environmental

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: factors on the observed critical potentials of 18-8 stain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less steel in NaCl solutions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In view of the electrochemical mechanism of pit

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiation and growth, it is concluded that pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should be observed in aerated halide solutions, e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sea water, only in those metals and alloys whose crit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ical potentials lie below the reversible oxygen electrode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (approximately 0.8v in air). This is supported by data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of Table I listing critical potentials for several metals

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in 0.1N NaCl. In sea water (approximately 0.5N NaCl)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these values (1, 2) would be expected to be a few

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: centivolts more active. Metals such as Cr and Ti,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore, having critical potentials above 1v success-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fully resist pitting corrosion in aerated sea water in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: contrast to the other listed metals with values below

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.8v. The only exceptions that may arise in practice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: result from crevices at which stagnant electrolyte of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher CI- concentration accumulates because of elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trochemical transport (lowering the critical potential)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and, more importantly, of lower pH and dissolved O2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concentration causing localized breakdown of passiv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity (7). In general, the more noble the critical poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial, the more resistant is the metal to pitting attack.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: But how fast pits grow once initiated usually depends

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on rate of the cathodic reaction, which in aerated NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is dependent on rate of O2 diffusion and reduction. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over-all rate, in turn, is a function of available total

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cathode surface (8) and conductivity of the electrolyte.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, the effect of alloying on the critical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentials of the Cr-Fe-Ni-Mo system in aqueous NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution is reported, first as exhibited by several binary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys and then by some of the ternary and quaternary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys of the usual stainless alloy compositions. Data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also include an interesting, perhaps unexpected, effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of temperature on the critical potentials of stainless

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels containing alloyed Mo.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Experimental Procedure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloys were prepared in the laboratory from pure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: components by vacuum melting in dense alumina cru-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cibles. After allowing A or He to enter the furnace the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: melt was drawn into 7 mm diam Vycor tubes and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quenched in water. The ingots were homogenized in A

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or He, usually at 1050°-1100°C for several hours after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which each composition was determined chemically.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ingots of Ni-Cr, Ni-Mo, and Cr-Fe were cold rolled

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to 0.25 cm, then annealed at 1000°-1050°C and water

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quenched. The Cr-Fe alloys containing more than 40%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Cr were difficult to roll or swage, hence electrodes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were machined directly from the homogenized ingot.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ingots of the lower % Cr-Fe alloys and of the stain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: less steels were swaged to about 0.45 cm diam rods,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annealed at 1050°C, and water quenched.² All elec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trodes measured approximately 2 cm long and were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either 0.4 cm diam or 0.5 cm wide by 0.2 cm thick.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: They were mounted as described earlier (2) by a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: threaded member allowing attachment to a nickel

layout_dets.text: " A subsequent anneal after quenching to avoid intergranular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: usually in 15% HNO3, 5% HF at 80°C for 5 min to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Iron used for the melts was electrolytic grade, first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deoxidized then decarburized in H2 to approximately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 0.001-0.002% C. Chromium was of special high purity

layout_dets.text: obtained from Union Carbide Company. Carbonyl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: national Nickel Company. Molybdenum was 99.9%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and for some few alloys it was spectroscopic grade,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but without differing results.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The electrolyte for most experiments was 0.1N NaCl

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deaerated with purified nitrogen (passed over Cu at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: but without flow of nitrogen during the time

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of actual measurements. The Pyrex cell, fitted with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground glass joints as described previously (2), was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: located in an air thermostat maintained at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which could also be adjusted to constant temperatures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher or lower than room temperature. A Wenking

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potentiostat was employed in conjunction with a chart

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recorder. The electrolyte was usually maintained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: above the Teflon gasket-electrode interface. Several

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: comparative measurements were made holding the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrolyte below the Teflon gasket allowing a menis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cus to form at the gas-liquid interface. Under condi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions of continuous potential sweep, such critical po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tentials were found in general to be higher (more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: noble) than for total immersion. However, for long-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time or steady-state conditions, values tended to focus

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the same potential for partially or totally im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mersed electrodes, hence in view of the shorter times

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: needed to achieve steady state under conditions of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: total immersion, it was this procedure which was usu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ally followed. Pitting was observed to initiate prefer-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ably at the Teflon-electrode interface, but was not re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stricted to such areas in long-time polarization runs.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The experimental procedure was to first polarize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the electrode potentiostatically at the least noble po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tential within the passive region for at least 15 min

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in order to achieve steady-state passivity. The poten-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tial was then advanced in stages of 50 mv, allowing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 min between each change. Initially the current de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: creased or remained constant after each potential ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: justment, but eventually a steadily increasing current

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at some potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicated the onset of pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (or of transpassivity). Steady-state values

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: obtained subsequently by holding the potential for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: long times at a fixed value and then observing pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or the lack of it under a low power microscope. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lowest potential for which pitting could not be ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: served after a 10-hr or longer period of constant po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larization was considered to be the steady-state value

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reproducibility was in the order of ±5 mv.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The basic mechanism accounting for the critical po-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adsorbingcompeti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively with oxygen of the passive film for sites on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metal surface. As the potential is made more noble,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ions move into the double layer of the electrode

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: surface, eventually reaching at the critical potential

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the concentration required to displace adsorbed oxy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gen (or an oxygen-H2O complex) at favored locations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for adsorbed oxygen, thereby initiating a pit. This is
